tweets.title: The more I understand mountain logistics and high-altitude warfare, the more I appreciate what the Indian Army accomplished. If push comes to shove, the Indian Army can undoubtedly undertake such missions even today. In many ways, it would be comparatively easier, thanks to far better surveillance, precision weapons, aviation assets, communications, and logistics. What truly stands out, however, is the resilience of that generation. Today, with 24/7 media coverage and social media broadcasting every setback in real time, it’s difficult to imagine a society accepting the kind of losses that were once endured to accomplish larger goal “The mission”.

tweets.content:
Geography often dictates geopolitical destiny of Nations. For India it is Siliguri Corridor, it is mere 22km wide, yet it anchors the economic and strategic fate of 45 million citizens in India's Northeast. It stands as a stark reminder of how critical domestic infrastructure vulnerabilities can intersect directly with complex international frontiers.

Netram Defence Review (@NetramDefence)

THREAD🧵

Significance of Siliguri Corridor

Few geographical features carry as much strategic importance as the Siliguri Corridor, popularly known as the “Chicken’s Neck.” This narrow strip of land in northern West Bengal is the only continuous land bridge connecting mainland India to its eight northeastern states. Every military planner, policymaker and strategist recognizes it as one of India’s most critical national security vulnerabilities.
